name: Haush
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro & Marisa Malvestitti. 2019. Apéndice: Datos haush ('Ona') del manuscrito. Indiana 36(2): A117-A137. DOI 10.18441/ind.v36i2.A117-A137.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Raw 1882 Spegazzini/Lafone Quevedo data in original spelling; no accent marks or remarks.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro. 2015. Proto-Chon: fonología, morfología y léxico. Tesis doctoral, Universidad de Buenos Aires, Facultad de Filosofía y Letras, vol. 1 (303 pp.). Repositorio FFyL-UBA hdl filodigital/3013.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. IV §5 'Fenómenos suprasegmentales', p. 150 (PDF p. 171): 'Para el teushen y el haush, las fuentes presentan en general pocos datos sobre el acento, pero no dicen nada sobre la posible existencia de tono en estas lenguas.' The accent subsections (§5.1.1-5.1.3) cover only Selknam, Tehuelche and Teushen; §1.3 'Fonemización tentativa del haush' (pp. 101-102) gives consonants/vowels only, no accent. §1.1.1.1 (pp. 14-15) lists all known Haush sources (about 300 distinct words, 3 sentences).
No phonology or stress information; cites Adelaar & Muysken 2004, Furlong 1917 (ICA) and the Indiana 2019 article.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro & Marisa Malvestitti. 2019. Un manuscrito de Carlos Spegazzini con datos inéditos sobre la lengua haush. Indiana 36(2): 101-128. DOI 10.18441/ind.v36i2.101-128.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 'Aspectos fonéticos y fonológicos' (pp. 112-113) discusses only epenthetic homorganic stops after nasals and epenthetic vowels; nothing on accent/stress (the only 'acento' hit is 'acento gutural' in a quoted 19th-c. description).

sources.citation: Bridges, E. Lucas. 1948. Uttermost part of the earth. London: Hodder & Stoughton (Digital Library of India scan on archive.org).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic memoir; Aush (Eastern Ona) mentioned as a distinct language; no linguistic description of stress.

sources.citation: Furlong, Charles Wellington. 1917. Tribal distribution and settlements of the Fuegians, comprising nomenclature, etymology, philology, and populations. Geographical Review 3(3): 169-187 (archive.org scan of vol. 3).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only 'in respect of its harsh and guttural nature the Haushan resembled the Onan tongue'; notes Bridges' 500-600-word 'Eastern Ona' manuscript vocabulary; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lehmann-Nitsche, Robert. 1913. El grupo lingüístico Tshon de los territorios magallánicos. Revista del Museo de La Plata 22: 217-276 (archive.org scan of the volume bound with Hunt, El vejoz ó aiyo).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 238 orthographic key for the comparative Tshon vocabulary: 'Un apóstrofe después de a, o, ü, significa acento'; column 'M. = Mánekenkn de Bridges' carries Bridges' Haush list (c. 115 words), in which no accent apostrophes are visible in the scanned; no statement on Haush stress.

sources.citation: Lista, Ramón. 1887. Viaje al país de los onas, Tierra del Fuego. Buenos Aires: A. Núñez.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Brief remarks on vowels and guttural consonants of 'Ona' (pp. 81-82) and a Bahía Thetis (Haush) wordlist p. 144; no statement on accent.

sources.citation: Regúnaga, María Alejandra & Matthias Pache. 2024. Un vocabulario del haush, lengua extinta de Tierra del Fuego: Comentarios y transcripción del manuscrito inédito de Martin Gusinde (1919). Anthropos 119(2): 355-415.

sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Largest Haush source ever edited (50-page Gusinde manuscript, 60-page article) with an explicit discussion of transcription conventions; the one place a modern statement on accent marking in Haush could appear. Restricted on Nomos/inlibra and on CONICET Digital (hdl 11336/296540).
